description: Teach the catalogue which MIDI message a control really sends: after the user moved one control on the device (see relay_listen), give the driver address it is (from list_routes) — or, for a control the driver lacks, its panel label — and the CC, NRPN or note it sent, with the firmware and the device's Identity Reply when you have them. When several accounts observe the same thing on one firmware the mapping is learned; get_trust shows learned mappings and where they differ from the driver. For a device with no driver, the first step of its first driver: the person gives its vendor, model and firmware, and you map its controls one by one with device set to its vendor/model id (the slugs of the vendor and the model, e.g. behringer/bcr-32); the mappings then make the first driver you send with submit_driver.

address.description: The driver's OSC address for the control.

device.description: Driver id or OSC prefix; for a device with no driver yet, its vendor/model id as its fingerprint was shared (e.g. behringer/bcr-32).

identity_hex.description: The device's reply to the MIDI Identity Request, in hex.

label.description: The control's panel label, when the driver has no address for it.

user_id.description: Your anonymous SyntHub id, if you kept it from an earlier session (see the server instructions). Optional.

name: report_mapping
